scope: Published main-body content in the 14 /blog/*/index.html article pages; template and blog landing page excluded.

claims.claim: BasicMed aircraft/passenger limits were 6,000 lb, six occupants, five passengers.
claims.source: FAA, 'FAA Updates BasicMed Program' (Nov. 15, 2024), BasicMed expansion.
claims.finding: Incorrect after the 2024 expansion: 12,500 lb, seven occupants, and six passengers (with the stated helicopter exception).
claims.changes: Corrected limits and linked the FAA source.

claims.claim: Sport Pilots are limited to the former LSA definition, daytime only, two seats, and cannot use a Cessna 172.
claims.source: FAA, Sport Pilot page, 'Key Changes' effective Oct. 22, 2025; FAA MOSAIC page.
claims.finding: Outdated after MOSAIC. Aircraft criteria are now in 14 CFR 61.316; night may be available with training, endorsements, and medical qualification.
claims.changes: Replaced legacy checklist and categorical C172 answer with current-rule verification language and FAA links.

claims.claim: Former 1,320-lb/120-knot/two-seat LSA definition determines Sport Pilot eligibility; local wet rates and fixed NG5 specification apply generally.
claims.source: FAA, MOSAIC page; FAA, Sport Pilot page, effective dates and 14 CFR 61.316 transition.
claims.finding: Legacy Sport Pilot test is obsolete; configuration, certification records, endorsements, and live operator pricing are aircraft-specific.
claims.changes: Removed unsupported generic NG5 specifications and local price figures; revised LSA/Sport Pilot treatment and linked FAA MOSAIC guidance.

claims.claim: A dual discovery-flight lesson may be logged toward a later certificate.
claims.source: 14 CFR 61.51, pilot logbooks; 14 CFR 61.109, private-pilot aeronautical experience.
claims.finding: Accurate when the flight time is properly logged and otherwise meets the applicable requirement.
claims.changes: No change; operational offering durations are presented as estimates, not regulatory facts.

claims.claim: Student solo, cross-country, knowledge-test, practical-test, flight-review, and IPC endorsements have distinct conditions and expirations.
claims.source: FAA AC 61-65K, endorsement appendices; 14 CFR 61.87, 61.93, 61.56, and 61.57.
claims.finding: Accurate high-level explanation; page points readers to AC 61-65K rather than substituting generic wording.

claims.claim: An instructor endorsement is required before the Private Pilot knowledge test and passing it is required before the practical test.
claims.source: 14 CFR 61.35(a)(1) and 61.103(d); FAA Airman Certification Standards resources.
claims.changes: No change; provider and scheduling details are framed as local logistics.

claims.claim: FAA knowledge tests are scheduled through PSI and require an FTN and appropriate endorsement or graduation certificate.
claims.source: FAA Airman Knowledge Testing, applicant process; 14 CFR 61.35.
claims.finding: Accurate at review; test-center availability and fees are variable.
claims.changes: No change; page directs readers to verify scheduling live.

claims.claim: KLOU Class D and adjacent SDF Class C procedures affect local operations.
claims.source: FAA Chart Supplement and current FAA sectional/chart data; current NOTAM system.
claims.finding: Airport and airspace details are inherently chart/NOTAM controlled and must be verified before flight.
claims.changes: No change to instructional overview; existing official-resource direction retained.

claims.claim: Part 61 and Part 141 differ in regulatory structure and training requirements.
claims.source: 14 CFR parts 61 and 141; FAA Become a Pilot guidance.
claims.finding: Accurate as a high-level comparison; costs, scheduling, and instructor availability are recommendations rather than fixed facts.

claims.claim: Derby-week flight restrictions and procedures must be checked every year.
claims.source: FAA NOTAM Search and event-specific FAA special-flight-procedures notices.
claims.finding: Accurate and appropriately non-static; an annual event does not create a standing reusable TFR.

claims.claim: Pattern work, go-around decisions, and runway use are training subjects.
claims.source: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook and current FAA Chart Supplement/ATC instructions for runway and pattern operations.
claims.finding: Educational guidance does not purport to replace current ATC instructions or airport data.

claims.claim: MedXPress is the FAA medical application used before an AME examination; deferral is not itself a denial.
claims.source: FAA MedXPress and FAA Guide for Aviation Medical Examiners.
claims.finding: Accurate. Individual medical eligibility and processing time cannot be predicted from a general article.
claims.changes: No change; medical guidance remains educational rather than diagnostic.

claims.claim: Airplane CFI applicants need the prerequisites in 14 CFR 61.183, including the relevant commercial/ATP, instrument, spin-training, and PIC requirements.
claims.source: 14 CFR 61.183 and 61.185; FAA Aviation Instructor's Handbook.
claims.finding: Accurate high-level summary. Stated time/cost ranges are planning estimates, not FAA requirements.

claims.claim: Private Pilot minimum experience is 40 hours; actual local total cost varies with hours, operator rates, instruction, and equipment.
claims.source: 14 CFR 61.109(a); FAA Become a Pilot guidance.
claims.finding: 40 hours is the regulatory minimum. Local price ranges are explicitly labeled estimates and must be refreshed against operator quotes.

claims.claim: Private Pilot minimum is 40 hours and BasicMed requires a medical certificate valid after July 14, 2006.
claims.finding: Accurate. The 6-to-12-month and weather/DPE examples are planning estimates, not FAA-set outcomes.
